title: GPU IaC consistency and migration playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview:

This playbook documents the safe, repeatable process for migrating GPU-related Terraform/IaC modules, account/region moves, and network/egress changes while preserving fleet capacity, tenant isolation, and cost-accounting integrity. It focuses on the cross-cutting concerns between GPU fleet & capacity, cloud accounts and networking, Terraform module compatibility, CI/CD gates, and runbook procedures for both planned migrations and emergency rollbacks.

Why this exists:
- GPU infrastructure is a critical shared resource with hard SLOs for latency and throughput; IaC changes that alter placement, tags, or networking can silently impact tenant routing or billing.
- Migrations happen frequently (module refactors, account consolidation, region expansion). We need a single canonical checklist and tooling set to avoid regressions.

Scope and ownership:
- Applies to: Terraform modules that affect GPU pools, node groups, VPC/subnet changes, NAT/egress routing, IAM for tenant access, and autoscaler policies.
- Excludes: application-layer deployment manifests (handled by service teams) and model artifacts.
- Primary owner: eng-infra (Terraform/IaC team). Secondary stakeholders: eng-sre (capacity), eng-platform (autoscaler & routing), customer-success (tenant SLA communication).

Key SLO and thresholds to consider before migration:
- 99th-percentile latency for inference routing < 120ms external, < 30ms internal routing.
- Warm-pool replenishment time <= 90s for spot-backed pools.
- Tenant allocation error rate < 0.1% during migration window.
- Cost accounting accuracy: tag coverage >= 99.5% for migrated resources.

Pre-migration checklist (gated, run by CI and runbook lead):
1) Module compatibility matrix: confirm new module supports previous input variables and outputs or provide adapter wrapper.
2) Automated tfsec/terrascan scan: no high or critical findings.
3) Unit test harness: terraform plan for every target account & region in staging.
4) Synthetic workload test: run 1–2 hour canary load against staging GPU pool; measure token/sec and tail latency.
5) Tag and billing preflight: run tag-coverage report and cost-mapping for current resources.
6) Network path validation: confirm VPC/subnet route tables, NACLs, and NAT gateways are configured with the same egress IP pools expected by tenants.
7) Backfill policy prepared: documented plan to reassign warm pool seeds across pools if node counts shift.
8) Rollout window and oncall: schedule a low-traffic window, confirm oncall rotation for eng-infra and eng-sre.

CI/CD guards and automation patterns:
- Pipeline stages (must pass to deploy): lint -> unit plan (single-account) -> cross-account plan (matrix) -> apply-preview with dry-run -> canary apply -> smoke tests -> promote to full apply.
- Use pipeline feature-flag gating: experimental module releases must be behind feature flags toggled via remote-state feature-flags.tfvars.
- Terraform state handling: use remote state locks with cross-account s3/backends and explicit restore points (incremental snapshots).
- Promotion policy: canary region must pass 2x duration of historical warmup (default 30m) before global promotion.

Safe migration pattern (high level):
1) Prepare module adapter: create a lightweight wrapper that maps old outputs to the new module’s outputs to maintain service references.
2) Deploy adapter to staging account and run end-to-end smoke tests.
3) Run canary apply in non-critical region/account with 10% of traffic routed. Monitor for 2x warmup period.
4) Gradual expansion: 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over successive windows, with health checks holding at each step.
5) Finalize: remove adapter and rotate state if necessary.

Runbook: immediate operator actions for migration failures
- Symptom: provisioning errors during apply, or live traffic errors (tenant open connections failing), or spike in allocation errors.
Quick remediation steps (ordered):
1) Abort any in-progress apply (CI cancels).
2) Revert routing to previous pool via smart-routing fallback policy (console: Route -> rollback -> fallback-policy:previous).
3) If TF state is inconsistent: restore state snapshot from pre-migration snapshot (s3://redwood-iac-snapshots/<snapshot-id>) and run terraform refresh in a dry-run workspace.
4) If nodes are unhealthy: mark affected node groups as unschedulable and trigger warm-pool seeding to alternate pools.
5) Open incident and notify oncall_eng_infra@redwood.com; include terraform plan, apply logs, and cloud provider API request IDs.

Detailed verification checks (post-apply):
- Terraform diff: zero unexpected resource deletions.
- Tag verification: run tagging check script (scripts/check-tags.sh) -> expect all new resources have tags: team, cost_center, env, purpose, tenant_group.
- Network egress test: curl from a probe in the GPU subnet to the telemetry endpoint and compare egress IP to expected pools.
- Autoscaler sanity: force a small burst and confirm scale-up < 60s and warm-pool fill < 90s.
- Billing sanity: run cost ingestion preview and ensure new resource consumption maps to correct billing tag.

Sample Terraform variable table (ASCII):
+----------------------+----------------------+---------------------------------+
| variable             | default              | notes                           |
+----------------------+----------------------+---------------------------------+
| region               | "us-west-2"         | deployment region                |
| instance_type        | "p4d.24xlarge"      | fallback instance type           |
| warm_pool_min        | "2"                 | minimum warm nodes per tenant    |
| tenancy_tag          | "gpu-shared"        | used for cost allocation         |
| egress_subnet_cidr   | "10.20.32.0/24"     | NAT/egress subnet for probes     |
+----------------------+----------------------+---------------------------------+

Example terraform plan command (recommended):
- TF_WORKSPACE=staging terraform plan -var-file=env/staging.tfvars -out=plan.tfplan
- TF_LOG=info terraform show -json plan.tfplan | jq '.resource_changes[] | select(.change.actions != ["no-op"])'

Troubleshooting snippets:
- Recovering leaked instances: aws ec2 describe-instances --filters "Name=tag:git_sha,Values=<sha>" | jq '.Reservations[].Instances[] | {InstanceId, State, Tags}'
- Verifying remote state lock: aws dynamodb get-item --table-name tf-locks --key '{"LockID":{"S":"<lock-id>"}}'

Monitoring and dashboards to observe during migration:
- GPU-pool-health dashboard: replica count, average startup time, allocation error rate. Alert if allocation error rate > 0.1% for 5m.
- Network-e2e: probe success rate to telemetry endpoint; alert if < 99.5% over 5m.
- Cost-tagging: daily tag-coverage metric; alert if < 99% for 24h.

Post-migration validation and housekeeping:
- Run a 24–72 hour drift detection job: terraform plan against all accounts/regions and file PR for any unexpected drift.
- Clean up legacy resources and adapters once 30 days of stable metrics.
- Update module changelog and increment semantic version.
- Run brownout simulation (traffic reduction) to ensure graceful degradation works with new topology.
